# Foundations Principles {.unnumbered}

Part I establishes the architectural and theoretical foundations of agentic machine learning systems. Moving beyond stateless token generation, we define the closed-loop autonomous trajectory, construct the Agent Control Block (ACB) as the core operating system descriptor for non-stationary belief states, and formalize control topologies that bound non-deterministic reasoning into finite, dependable execution graphs.

::: {#pri-vol3-trajectory-encapsulation .callout-principle title="Trajectory-level encapsulation"}

**Invariant**: The atomic unit of execution, resource allocation, and safety enforcement is not the token or the request, but the multi-step trajectory bounded by an invariant-enforcing runtime.

**Implication**: Runtimes must track and enforce budgets, capabilities, and rollbacks at the trajectory boundary rather than across isolated stateless requests.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-acb-binding .callout-principle title="Descriptor-bounded authority"}

**Invariant**: Autonomous execution requires a kernel-managed descriptor tracking principal identity, dynamic token allowances, and capability leases across non-stationary memory.

**Implication**: State management must decouple internal neural activations in GPU memory from authoritative external permission and budget ledgers.

:::

::: {#pri-vol3-bounded-execution .callout-principle title="Bounded dynamic execution"}

**Invariant**: Stochastic reasoning loops must be bounded by deterministic state machine topologies; cycles require semantic progress metrics and automated circuit breakers.

**Implication**: Runtimes must reject unconstrained peer-to-peer swarms in favor of structured supervisor trees that guarantee forward progress.

:::
